api_types.name: Port
api_types.doc: Port defines the network port that will be exposed by this InferencePool.

fields.name: Number
fields.doc: Number defines the port number to access the selected model server Pods. The number must be in the range 1 to 65535.

api_types.name: EndpointPickerRef
api_types.doc: EndpointPickerRef specifies a reference to an Endpoint Picker extension and its associated configuration.

fields.name: Group
fields.doc: Group is the group of the referent API object. When unspecified, the default value is "", representing the Core API group.

fields.name: Kind
fields.doc: Kind is the Kubernetes resource kind of the referent. Required if the referent is ambiguous, e.g. service with multiple ports. Defaults to "Service" when not specified. ExternalName services can refer to CNAME DNS records that may live outside of the cluster and as such are difficult to reason about in terms of conformance. They also may not be safe to forward to (see CVE-2021-25740 for more information). Implementations MUST NOT support ExternalName Services.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the name of the referent API object.

fields.name: Port
fields.doc: Port is the port of the Endpoint Picker extension service. Port is required when the referent is a Kubernetes Service. In this case, the port number is the service port number, not the target port. For other resources, destination port might be derived from the referent resource or this field.

fields.name: FailureMode
fields.doc: FailureMode configures how the parent handles the case when the Endpoint Picker extension is non-responsive. When unspecified, defaults to "FailClose".

markers: +kubebuilder:validation:XValidation:rule="self.kind != 'Service' || has(self.port)",message="port is required when kind is 'Service' or unspecified (defaults to 'Service')"

api_types.name: InferencePoolStatus
api_types.doc: InferencePoolStatus defines the observed state of the InferencePool.

fields.name: Parents
fields.doc: Parents is a list of parent resources, typically Gateways, that are associated with the InferencePool, and the status of the InferencePool with respect to each parent. A controller that manages the InferencePool, must add an entry for each parent it manages and remove the parent entry when the controller no longer considers the InferencePool to be associated with that parent. A maximum of 32 parents will be represented in this list. When the list is empty, it indicates that the InferencePool is not associated with any parents. +listType=atomic

api_types.name: ParentStatus
api_types.doc: ParentStatus defines the observed state of InferencePool from a Parent, i.e. Gateway.

fields.name: Conditions
fields.doc: Conditions is a list of status conditions that provide information about the observed state of the InferencePool. This field is required to be set by the controller that manages the InferencePool. Supported condition types are: * "Accepted" * "ResolvedRefs" +listType=map +listMapKey=type

fields.name: ParentRef
fields.doc: ParentRef is used to identify the parent resource that this status is associated with. It is used to match the InferencePool with the parent resource, such as a Gateway.

fields.name: ControllerName
fields.doc: ControllerName is a domain/path string that indicates the name of the controller that wrote this status. This corresponds with the GatewayClass controllerName field when the parentRef references a Gateway kind. Example: "example.net/gateway-controller". The format of this field is DOMAIN "/" PATH, where DOMAIN and PATH are valid Kubernetes names: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names Controllers MAY populate this field when writing status. When populating this field, controllers should ensure that entries to status populated with their ControllerName are cleaned up when they are no longer necessary.

fields.name: Status
fields.doc: Status defines the observed state of the InferencePool. nolint:kubeapilinter // status should not be a pointer.

api_types.name: ParentReference
api_types.doc: ParentReference identifies an API object. It is used to associate the InferencePool with a parent resource, such as a Gateway.

fields.name: Group
fields.doc: Group is the group of the referent API object. When unspecified, the referent is assumed to be in the "gateway.networking.k8s.io" API group.

fields.name: Kind
fields.doc: Kind is the kind of the referent API object. When unspecified, the referent is assumed to be a "Gateway" kind.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is the name of the referent API object.

fields.name: Namespace
fields.doc: Namespace is the namespace of the referenced object. When unspecified, the local namespace is inferred. Note that when a namespace different than the local namespace is specified, a ReferenceGrant object is required in the referent namespace to allow that namespace's owner to accept the reference. See the ReferenceGrant documentation for details: https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/api-types/referencegrant/

api_types.name: InferencePoolList
api_types.doc: InferencePoolList contains a list of InferencePools.

api_types.name: InferencePoolSpec
api_types.doc: InferencePoolSpec defines the desired state of the InferencePool.

fields.name: Selector
fields.doc: Selector determines which Pods are members of this inference pool. It matches Pods by their labels only within the same namespace; cross-namespace selection is not supported. The structure of this LabelSelector is intentionally simple to be compatible with Kubernetes Service selectors, as some implementations may translate this configuration into a Service resource.

fields.name: TargetPorts
fields.doc: TargetPorts defines a list of ports that are exposed by this InferencePool. Every port will be treated as a distinctive endpoint by EPP, addressable as a 'podIP:portNumber' combination. +listType=atomic
markers: +kubebuilder:validation:XValidation:message="port number must be unique",rule="self.all(p1, self.exists_one(p2, p1.number==p2.number))"

fields.name: AppProtocol
fields.doc: AppProtocol describes the application protocol for all the target ports. If unspecified, the protocol defaults to HTTP/1.1. Supported values include: * "http": HTTP/1.1. This is the default. * "kubernetes.io/h2c": HTTP/2 over cleartext.

fields.name: EndpointPickerRef
fields.doc: EndpointPickerRef is a reference to the Endpoint Picker extension and its associated configuration.

api_types.name: LabelSelector
api_types.doc: LabelSelector defines a query for resources based on their labels. This simplified version uses only the matchLabels field.

fields.name: MatchLabels
fields.doc: MatchLabels contains a set of required {key,value} pairs. An object must match every label in this map to be selected. The matching logic is an AND operation on all entries.

operator_config.name: AppProtocolH2C
operator_config.doc:
AppProtocolH2C represents HTTP/2 over cleartext (h2c).
This protocol is typically used for gRPC workloads where TLS is terminated
at the Gateway or not used within the cluster.

operator_config.name: AppProtocolHTTP
operator_config.doc:
AppProtocolHTTP represents the HTTP/1.1 protocol.
This is the default protocol if AppProtocol is unspecified.

operator_config.name: EndpointPickerFailClose
operator_config.doc:
EndpointPickerFailClose specifies that the parent should drop the request when the Endpoint
Picker extension fails.

operator_config.name: EndpointPickerFailOpen
operator_config.doc:
EndpointPickerFailOpen specifies that the parent should forward the request to an endpoint
of its picking when the Endpoint Picker extension fails.

operator_config.name: InferencePoolConditionAccepted
operator_config.doc:
InferencePoolConditionAccepted is a type of condition that indicates whether
the InferencePool has been accepted or rejected by a Parent, and why.

Possible reasons for this condition to be True are:

* "SupportedByParent"

Possible reasons for this condition to be False are:

* "Accepted"
* "HTTPRouteNotAccepted"

Possible reasons for this condition to be Unknown are:

* "Pending"

Controllers MAY raise this condition with other reasons, but should
prefer to use the reasons listed above to improve interoperability.

operator_config.name: InferencePoolConditionExported
operator_config.doc:
InferencePoolConditionExported is a type of condition that indicates whether the
controller was able to export the InferencePool to the specified clusters.

Possible reasons for this condition to be True are:

* "Exported"

Possible reasons for this condition to be False are:

* "NotRequested"
* "NotSupported"

Controllers MAY raise this condition with other reasons, but should
prefer to use the reasons listed above to improve interoperability.

operator_config.name: InferencePoolConditionResolvedRefs
operator_config.doc:
InferencePoolConditionResolvedRefs is a type of condition that indicates whether
the controller was able to resolve all the object references for the InferencePool.

Possible reasons for this condition to be True are:

* "ResolvedRefs"

Possible reasons for this condition to be False are:

* "InvalidExtensionRef"

Controllers MAY raise this condition with other reasons, but should
prefer to use the reasons listed above to improve interoperability.

operator_config.name: InferencePoolReasonAccepted
operator_config.doc:
InferencePoolReasonAccepted is a reason used with the "Accepted" condition
when the InferencePool is accepted by a Parent because the Parent supports
InferencePool as a backend.

operator_config.name: InferencePoolReasonExported
operator_config.doc:
InferencePoolReasonExported is a reason used with the "Exported" condition when the
condition is true.

operator_config.name: InferencePoolReasonHTTPRouteNotAccepted
operator_config.doc:
InferencePoolReasonHTTPRouteNotAccepted is an optional reason used with the
"Accepted" condition when the InferencePool is referenced by an HTTPRoute that
has been rejected by the Parent. The user should inspect the status of the
referring HTTPRoute for the specific reason.

operator_config.name: InferencePoolReasonInvalidExtensionRef
operator_config.doc:
InferencePoolReasonInvalidExtensionRef is a reason used with the "ResolvedRefs"
condition when the Extension is invalid in some way. This can include an
unsupported kind or API group, or a reference to a resource that cannot be found.

operator_config.name: InferencePoolReasonNotRequested
operator_config.doc:
InferencePoolReasonNotRequested is a reason used with the "Exported" condition when the
condition is false and no export was requested by the InferencePool. This indicates a
deliberate non-action rather than an error.

operator_config.name: InferencePoolReasonNotSupported
operator_config.doc:
InferencePoolReasonNotSupported is a reason used with the "Exported" condition when the
condition is false and the export was requested but is not supported by the implementation.
Controllers should include details in the condition message.

operator_config.name: InferencePoolReasonNotSupportedByParent
operator_config.doc:
InferencePoolReasonNotSupportedByParent is a reason used with the "Accepted"
condition when the InferencePool has not been accepted by a Parent because
the Parent does not support InferencePool as a backend.

operator_config.name: InferencePoolReasonResolvedRefs
operator_config.doc:
InferencePoolReasonResolvedRefs is a reason used with the "ResolvedRefs"
condition when the condition is true.

operator_config.name: AddToScheme
operator_config.doc:
AddToScheme adds all types of this clientset into the given scheme. This allows composition
of clientsets, like in:

	import (
	  "k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes"
	  clientsetscheme "k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/scheme"
	  aggregatorclientsetscheme "k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/client/clientset_generated/clientset/scheme"
	)

	kclientset, _ := kubernetes.NewForConfig(c)
	_ = aggregatorclientsetscheme.AddToScheme(clientsetscheme.Scheme)

After this, RawExtensions in Kubernetes types will serialize kube-aggregator types
correctly.

operator_config.doc: ErrFlowInstanceNotFound indicates that a requested flow instance (a `ManagedQueue`) does not exist.

operator_config.name: ErrInvalidQueueItemHandle
operator_config.doc:
ErrInvalidQueueItemHandle indicates that a QueueItemHandle provided to a SafeQueue operation (e.g.,
SafeQueue.Remove()) is not valid for that queue, has been invalidated, or does not correspond to an actual item in
the queue.

operator_config.name: ErrInvalidShardCount
operator_config.doc: ErrInvalidShardCount indicates that an invalid shard count was provided (e.g., zero or negative).

operator_config.name: ErrPolicyQueueIncompatible
operator_config.value: errors.New("policy is not compatible with queue capabilities")
operator_config.doc: ErrPolicyQueueIncompatible indicates that a selected policy is not compatible with the capabilities of the queue.

operator_config.name: ErrPriorityBandNotFound
operator_config.doc: ErrPriorityBandNotFound indicates that a requested priority band does not exist in the registry configuration.

operator_config.name: ErrQueueItemNotFound
operator_config.value: errors.New("queue item not found for the given handle")
operator_config.doc:
ErrQueueItemNotFound indicates that a SafeQueue.Remove(handle) operation did not find an item matching the
provided, valid QueueItemHandle. This can occur if the item was removed by a concurrent operation.

operator_config.name: ErrShardDraining
operator_config.doc:
ErrShardDraining indicates that an operation could not be completed because the target shard is in the process of
being gracefully drained. The caller should retry the operation on a different, Active shard.

operator_config.name: defaultEnqueueChannelBufferSize
operator_config.doc: defaultEnqueueChannelBufferSize is the default size of a worker's incoming request buffer.

operator_config.name: defaultExpiryCleanupInterval
operator_config.doc: defaultExpiryCleanupInterval is the default frequency for scanning for expired items.

operator_config.name: defaultProcessorReconciliationInterval
operator_config.doc: defaultProcessorReconciliationInterval is the default frequency for the supervisor loop.

operator_config.name: ErrProcessorBusy
operator_config.doc:
ErrProcessorBusy is a sentinel error returned by the processor's Submit method indicating that the processor's.
internal buffer is momentarily full and cannot accept new work.

operator_config.name: maxCleanupWorkers
operator_config.doc:
maxCleanupWorkers caps the number of concurrent workers for background cleanup tasks. This prevents a single shard
from overwhelming the Go scheduler with too many goroutines.

operator_config.name: RegisteredQueues
operator_config.doc: RegisteredQueues stores the constructors for all registered queues.

operator_config.name: ListQueueName
operator_config.doc:
ListQueueName is the name of the list-based queue implementation.

This queue provides a high-performance, low-overhead implementation based on a standard `container/list`.
It advertises the `CapabilityFIFO`.

# Behavioral Guarantees

The core guarantee of this queue is strict physical First-In, First-Out (FIFO) ordering. It processes items in the
exact order they are added to the queue on a specific shard.

# Performance and Trade-offs

Because the physical insertion order may not match a request's logical arrival time (due to the
`controller.FlowController`'s internal "bounce-and-retry" mechanic), this queue provides an*approximate FCFS behavior
from a system-wide perspective.

Given that true end-to-end ordering is non-deterministic in a distributed system, this high-performance queue is the
recommended default for most FCFS-like policies. It prioritizes throughput and efficiency, which aligns with the
primary goal of the Flow Control system.

For workloads that require the strictest possible logical-time ordering this layer can provide, explicitly using a
queue that supports `CapabilityPriorityConfigurable` is the appropriate choice.

operator_config.name: MaxMinHeapName
operator_config.doc: MaxMinHeapName is the name of the max-min heap queue implementation.

operator_config.name: DefaultFairnessPolicyRef
operator_config.doc: DefaultFairnessPolicyRef is the default policy for selecting which flow's queue to service next.

operator_config.name: DefaultOrderingPolicyRef
operator_config.doc: DefaultOrderingPolicyRef is the default policy for selecting items within a single flow's queue.

operator_config.name: DefaultUsageLimitPolicyRef
operator_config.doc: DefaultUsageLimitPolicyRef is the default policy to compute usage limit of a priority band dynamically.

operator_config.name: defaultFlowGCTimeout
operator_config.doc:
defaultFlowGCTimeout is the default duration of inactivity after which an idle flow is garbage collected.
This also serves as the interval for the periodic garbage collection scan.

operator_config.name: defaultInitialShardCount
operator_config.doc: defaultInitialShardCount is the default number of parallel shards to create when the registry is initialized.

operator_config.name: defaultPriorityBandGCTimeout
operator_config.doc:
defaultPriorityBandGCTimeout is the default duration of inactivity after which a dynamically provisioned
priority band is garbage collected. Set to 2x flow GC timeout to ensure flows are cleaned up first.

operator_config.name: defaultPriorityBandMaxBytes
operator_config.doc:
defaultPriorityBandMaxBytes is the default global capacity for a priority band if not explicitly configured.
It is set to 1 GB.

operator_config.name: defaultQueue
operator_config.doc: defaultQueue is the default queue implementation for flows.

operator_config.name: ErrContextCancelled
operator_config.doc:
ErrContextCancelled indicates a request was evicted because its associated context (from
`FlowControlRequest.Context()`) was cancelled. This error typically wraps the underlying `context.Canceled` or
`context.DeadlineExceeded` error.

operator_config.name: ErrEvicted
operator_config.doc:
ErrEvicted is a sentinel error indicating a request was removed from a queue *after* being successfully enqueued,
but for reasons other than successful dispatch (e.g., TTL expiry, displacement). Errors returned by
`FlowController.EnqueueAndWait()` that signify post-queue eviction will wrap this error.

Callers should use `errors.Is(err, ErrEvicted)` to check for this general class of failure.

operator_config.name: ErrFlowControllerNotRunning
operator_config.doc:
ErrFlowControllerNotRunning indicates that an operation could not complete or an item was evicted because the
`controller.FlowController` is not running or is in the process of shutting down.

When returned by `FlowController.EnqueueAndWait()`, this will be wrapped by `ErrRejected` (if rejection happens
before internal queuing) or `ErrEvicted` (if eviction happens after internal queuing).

operator_config.name: ErrQueueAtCapacity
operator_config.doc: ErrQueueAtCapacity indicates that a request could not be enqueued because queue capacity limits were met.

operator_config.name: ErrRejected
operator_config.doc:
ErrRejected is a sentinel error indicating a request was rejected by the `controller.FlowController` *before* being
formally enqueued. Errors returned by `FlowController.EnqueueAndWait()` that signify pre-queue rejection will wrap
this error.

Callers should use `errors.Is(err, ErrRejected)` to check for this general class of failure.

operator_config.name: ErrTTLExpired
operator_config.doc: ErrTTLExpired indicates a request was evicted from a queue because its effective Time-To-Live expired.

operator_config.name: ErrIncompatiblePriorityType
operator_config.value: errors.New("incompatible priority score type for comparison")
operator_config.doc:
ErrIncompatiblePriorityType indicates that a FairnessPolicy attempted to compare items from two different flow
queues whose ItemComparators have different ScoreType values, making a meaningful comparison impossible.

operator_config.name: CapabilityFIFO
operator_config.doc:
CapabilityFIFO indicates that the queue operates in a First-In, First-Out manner.
PeekHead() will return the oldest item (by logical enqueue time).

operator_config.name: CapabilityPriorityConfigurable
operator_config.doc:
CapabilityPriorityConfigurable indicates that the queue's ordering is determined by an ItemComparator.
PeekHead() will return the highest priority item, and PeekTail() will return the lowest priority item according to
this comparator.

operator_config.name: cleanupInterval
operator_config.doc: cleanupInterval defines the periodic interval that the cleanup go routine uses to check for stale data.

operator_config.name: stalenessThreshold
operator_config.doc:
stalenessThreshold defines the threshold for considering data as stale.
if data of a request hasn't been read/write in the last "stalenessThreshold", it is considered as stale data
and will be cleaned in the next cleanup cycle.

operator_config.name: Registry
operator_config.doc: Registry is a mapping from plugin name to Factory function

operator_config.name: ErrNotFound
operator_config.doc: ErrNotFound is the not found error message.

operator_config.name: Affinity
operator_config.doc:
Affinity indicates a scorer that prefers endpoints with existing locality, such as kv-cache or session-related state,
and therefore tends to give higher scores to the same endpoints.

operator_config.name: Balance
operator_config.doc: Balance indicates a scorer that its preference is balanced between Affinity and Distribution.

operator_config.name: Distribution
operator_config.doc:
Distribution indicates a scorer that prefers spreading requests evenly across all candidate endpoints to avoid
hotspots and improve overall utilization.

operator_config.name: ModalityImage
operator_config.doc: ModalityImage is the only currently supported modality.

operator_config.doc: defaultEngineName is the default engine used when defaultEngine is not specified.

operator_config.name: DefaultEngineType
operator_config.doc: DefaultEngineType is the key for the fallback mapping.

operator_config.name: DefaultEngineTypeLabelKey
operator_config.doc: DefaultEngineTypeLabelKey is the default label on Pods that indicates the inference engine type.

operator_config.name: defaultClient
maxIdleConnections
operator_config.doc:
the maximum idle connection count is shared by all endpoints. The value is
set high to ensure the number of idle connection is above the expected
endpoint count. Setting it too low would cause thrashing of the idle connection
pool and incur higher overheads for every GET (e.g., socket initiation, certificate
exchange, connections in timed wait state, etc.).

operator_config.name: maxIdleConnsPerHost
operator_config.doc:
allow some grace when connections are not made idle immediately (e.g., parsing
and updating might take some time). This allows maintaining up to two idle connections
per endpoint (defined as scheme://host:port).

operator_config.name: EndpointNotificationSourceType
operator_config.doc: EndpointNotificationSourceType is the plugin type identifier for endpoint notification sources.

operator_config.name: NotificationSourceType
operator_config.doc: NotificationSourceType is the plugin type identifier for k8s notification sources.

operator_config.name: SheddableFilterType
operator_config.doc:

operator_config.doc: defaultConfig provides sensible defaults for the prefix cache plugins.

operator_config.name: defaultLRUCapacityPerServer
operator_config.doc:
defaultLRUCapacityPerServer is the default capacity of the LRU indexer per server.
The indexer is an approximation to the actual prefix LRU cache state on the model servers per server (pod).
A small capacity ensures a high accuracy of cache hit on the model server, but it will
increase the chance of false negatives. A high capacity does the opposite.
To properly size this, consider the sum of the total number of cache entries on all model
servers. Consider the llama3 8B model on a H100 80GB GPUs. The size of the model weight is
about 16GB. The remaining HBM used for caching prefixes is 64GB. Each
token is about 128KB in size, so we can cache 500K tokens. Using the default block size of 16
in vLLM, we will have 250K / 16 = 31.25K blocks.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxPrefixBlocks
operator_config.doc:
defaultMaxPrefixBlocks is the maximum number of blocks to match.
Two long requests with the same prefix up to this limit will be indistinguishable.
This parameter provides a trade-off between cache size, prefix matching speed and matching
accuracy. Use a small value if most requests are short to reduce cache size and speed up the
matching process. Use a large value if most requests are long to increase the matching accuracy.

operator_config.name: experimentalDefaultPrefillProfile
operator_config.doc:
experimentalDefaultPrefillProfile is a hardcoded profile name for prefill nodes.
In P/D disaggregation mode, the prefill and decode are usually represented as two different
scheduling profiles to pick the prefill and decode endpoints. This constant defines the
prefill profile name to ensure that the index is updated for the prefill endpoint and not
only for the primary endpoint that will initially handle the request.
This is hardcoded for now until we land on a canonical approach for plugins to identify
prefill and decode endpoints (See https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api-inference-extension/issues/2080)
